newsitem.title: USA: Babbitt scraps effort to defend U.S. land agents.
newsitem.headline: Babbitt scraps effort to defend U.S. land agents.

text.p: Interior Secretary Bruce Babbitt Tuesday scrapped an attempt to quell the resentment and violence directed towards federal land agents in the West, saying the effort had only stirred up emotions even more.

Babbitt halted the effort by the Bureau of Land Management, which oversees vast land tracts in the West, to define and explain the power its agents have to enforce firearms laws and other rules on federal land.

"It's very clear that we have not done a good job of clarifying regulations and communicating BLM's legal authority under existing federal statutes to protect health, safety and environmental resources on America's public lands," he said.
Babbitt said in a statement the bureau would try to find another way to educate the public about its work.
"We learned there is a gross misunderstanding of what our responsiblities are and we have to do a better job of telling people what we do," Interior spokesman John Wright said.

BLM agents have become symbols in the perceived "War on the West," where irate Westerners accuse the federal government of heavy-handed intrusion over what they see as their rights to hunt, fish and make other use of federal land.

The BLM extended public comment periods twice on its proposal to consolidate and clarify its regulations, but Babbitt said the comments it received continued to show "confusion and misinformation" about the regulations.
